close_reason: Acceptable: cycle guard checks DN equality (names_match on subjects), which is the RFC 5280 name linkage criterion. Serial number check would be stronger but not required for correctness.
description:
**Issue**: The cycle guard in dfs() at pkix-path-builder/src/lib.rs:181-186 detects cycles by comparing the *subject name* of the candidate against subjects already in the path. This is the correct approach per RFC 4158.

However, it does not guard against a pool containing a self-signed certificate (subject == issuer) that is NOT the trust anchor. In this case:
1. path = [EE], EE.issuer = 'CN=SelfSigned'
2. Pool contains SelfSigned cert with subject='CN=SelfSigned', issuer='CN=SelfSigned', cA=TRUE
3. The dfs finds this cert as a candidate for EE (subject matches EE.issuer) — correct
4. Pushes it: path = [EE, SelfSigned]
5. Recurse: current_issuer = SelfSigned.issuer = 'CN=SelfSigned'
6. Check trust anchors: none match (SelfSigned is not an anchor)
7. Look for pool certs with subject='CN=SelfSigned': finds SelfSigned again
8. Cycle guard: SelfSigned.subject is already in path (at index 1) → SKIP (correct)
9. No other candidates → backtrack

So the cycle guard DOES prevent infinite loops in this case. The self-signed non-anchor cert is tried once, backtracked, and eventually build_path returns NoPathFound. This is correct behavior.

**Resolution**: No bug. The cycle guard correctly handles self-signed non-anchor pool certs. Document this case explicitly in the build_path doc comment, currently only documenting cycles detected by 'subject DNs already present in the path'.\n\n**Location**: pkix-path-builder/src/lib.rs:178-186\n\n**Fix**: Add a sentence to the doc comment: 'Self-signed certificates that are not trust anchors will be tried but immediately backtrack when the chain cannot extend further, avoiding infinite loops.'
title: build_path cycle guard checks subject not serial
